messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: pdx2-zonea inference-serving - error rate spike detected across several model pools. 5xx up ~6x, avg latency up from 45ms -> 420ms. Pager routed to @Priya (oncall). Root TS: 2318003456
Priya: saw the alert, ack'ing. currently pulling latest logs and checking autoscaler events. pinging @Eddie for runtime side.
Eddie: on it. initial look: gRPC connections dropping to the inference shards in pdx2-zonea. kube node restarts around 2318001200-2318003000. possible host kernel oom or driver flake. spinning up extra fallback replicas in west-us2 to offload.
Priya: activating mitigation runbook: 1) divert new requests from pdx2-zonea to west-us2 read-only variants; 2) scale up dedicated fallback cluster; 3) notify customers at risk. starting traffic diversion now.
Linh: routing rule change applied (canary) - `route-policy: region-fallback -> west-us2, weight: 80%` for affected model families. still allowing 20% to attempt local to observe errors.
Priya: can we confirm which customer tenants are hitting the affected model families? Alex, can support pull top-10 customers by RPS in the last hour for pdx2-zonea?
Alex: pulling list now. Top affected: AlphaHealth (prod), AcmeDocs (staging), EmberChat (prod), internal-loadtests. Drafting customer-facing note; will share shortly.
Eddie: kube events snapshot (excerpt):
```
23:08:12 kubelet: container runtime error: failed to start container
23:09:02 kubelet: OOMKilled process: queue_worker
23:10:45 node: kernel: i915: probe failed (gpu driver) -- GPU driver reset
23:12:00 autoscaler: attempted scale +3, failed due to image pull timeout
```
Not 100% sure it's GPU driver but pattern matches previous driver leak. opening host-level ticket for infra to investigate.
Priya: good to know. we need an internal comm for SRE/infra and a status page update. Linh can you spin up a short status snippet for the page? keep it concise and avoid blame.
Linh: posting status page draft below. feedback welcome.
```
Status: Degraded - Partial service disruption in pdx2-zonea
Impact: A subset of inference requests routed through pdx2-zonea may experience increased latency and intermittent errors. We are diverting traffic to fallback capacity in west-us2; most customers are already routed away.
ETA: Ongoing investigation; next update in 30 minutes.
```
Priya: LGTM. Alex — customer message draft? include steps customers can take (retry/backoff, prefer global endpoint) and link to status page.
Alex: posting customer notification draft (short email / in-app banner):
```
Subject: Service degradation affecting inference in pdx2-zonea
Body: Hi — we’re experiencing a partial degradation in our inference service affecting the pdx2-zonea region. You may see increased latency or occasional errors for requests served from that region. We are diverting traffic to healthy fallback capacity and estimating partial mitigation in the next 30–60 minutes. No action required on your side. If you rely on region-bound deployments, please contact support and we can assist with manual failover. Full updates: <status.redwood.ai/incidents/2318003456>
Regards, Redwood Inference Support
```
Priya: tidy. add note for enterprise customers: offer to rotate to dedicated capacity if SLA critical.
Comms-Bot: queued outbound notifications to enterprise contacts for AlphaHealth and EmberChat. will send once you confirm.
Priya: confirm send for AlphaHealth and EmberChat. AcmeDocs and internal tests - skip for now.
Marta: taking 2nd-avail handoff at 2318004800 — I’ll monitor and continue mitigation. Priya, leave any additional context before you go.
Priya: handoff notes: traffic diversion in place (80% west-us2), monitoring dashboards updated, pager alerts suppressed for diverted traffic. Key commands run: `redwood routing apply --policy pdx2-fallback --weight 80` and `kubectl -n inference scale deployment fallback-pool --replicas=10`. If the west-us2 fallback reaches >85% capacity, consider rapid scale to 20 replicas and enable burst queue.
Eddie: added host-level escalation ticket to infra (INC-4632) for driver investigation. linking logs and node IDs in ticket.
Marta: observed error rate drop from 6x to ~1.2x after diversion — latency improved to ~95–120ms for majority. some customers still show retries. continuing to monitor.
Linh: status page updated with the current ETA and a short blurb for external users. pushed page live at 2318005200.
Comms-Bot: outbound messages sent to enterprise contacts for AlphaHealth and EmberChat at 2318005300. copy of message stored in #customer-notices.
Alex: customer support playbook for incoming tickets: 1) confirm customer region, 2) check routing table, 3) advise retry/backoff and that we are diverting traffic, 4) offer migration to dedicated capacity if SLA-bound. pasteable snippet for agents: 
```
We’re aware of a partial service disruption impacting inference requests from the pdx2-zonea region. We are diverting traffic to fallback capacity and working on host-level remediation. You may see increased latency or retries. No action required unless you need region-specific guarantees; we can assist with forced failover.
```
Marta: infra reports driver patch candidate staged; plan to roll to affected hosts during a 10-min window with connection-drain. putting a hold on automated node reboots until after patch.
Eddie: once patch is rolled, we should validate KV cache warm-up and run perf smoke tests on a sample model family. schedule job: `smoke-test --region pdx2-zonea --models text-gen-2,chat-3`
Priya: thanks team. next scheduled update in 30m or earlier on notable changes. leaving the channel but I’m reachable via pager. :white_check_mark: 
Marta: taking point. will post final resolution and follow-up RCA timeline.
Incident Bot: UPDATE: traffic diversion applied. metrics back to partial-normal. next automated update in 15m.
